title: Coordinate retry window orchestration and idempotency metadata for multi-region failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Unify retry/timeout/backoff semantics across services and official SDKs to ensure safe hedged requests and deterministic de-duplication during multi-region failover. This ticket defines a canonical idempotency header, a bounded deduplication window, and a coordinated retry window that interacts with per-customer SLOs, circuit breakers, and load-shedding policies. The goal is to prevent duplicate side-effects during hedged requests, limit cross-region cascading retries, and make SDK behavior predictable for end-users and platform observability.
acceptance_criteria: Define canonical idempotency header name and serialization format (header + optional body hash) and document across SDKs
Server-side dedup window bounded and configurable: default 120s, configurable up to 24h for enterprise customers
SDKs implement 3 modes: optimistic (send idempotency key), canonicalize (derive key from normalized prompt+metadata), and strict (require user-supplied key).
Hedged-request controller enforces hedged fanout cap and per-request cumulative retry budget so multi-region failover does not exceed per-SLO token budget
Circuit breaker instrumentation propagates short-circuit status to SDKs and runtime so clients can fast-fail or route to fallback models
End-to-end tests covering: single-region transient failure, simultaneous region flapping, duplicate detection in presence of eventual KV-store replication lag
Migration plan and telemetry dashboard showing duplicate rate, dedup hit/miss, and customer-visible error surface before/after rollout
tasks: Draft idempotency header RFC and proto examples (Confluence)
Prototype server dedup store API and eviction TTL knobs
Add hedged-request governor to runtime: per-request budget & fanout cap
Update JS/Go/Python SDKs: canonicalization routine + config flags
Add observability: dedup counter, duplicate delta histogram, hedged fanout metric
Write integration tests (simulated multi-region latencies) and chaos experiment plan
Coordinate migration with Dedicated/Private teams to expose config controls in Console
notes: Motivation: customers reported duplicate webhook deliveries during regional failover for high-throughput workflows; root cause traced to uncoordinated SDK retries + no canonical idempotency key
Trade-offs discussed: long dedup window reduces duplicates but increases storage/memory costs; propose default 120s and enterprise knob up to 24h
Hedging model: prefer small, bounded fanout (max 2 regions concurrently) and cumulative retry budget derived from request SLO target

Open question: should dedup keys be stored in a global strongly-consistent store or use eventual replication with vector timestamps? Suggested path: start with single-region authoritative owner with replication and treat cross-region dedup as best-effort until runtime-1.20
Security: idempotency keys are not secrets but appear in logs; redact in high-sensitivity tenants and support tokenized key references for on-prem deployments
implementation_notes: Header name: X-RD-Idempotency (camel-cased for SDK consumers), fallback: x-rd-idempotency
Canonicalization: normalize whitespace, remove transient metadata fields (request_id, timestamp), stable-serialize JSON, then sha256() hex prefix 16 chars
Storage: use bounded LRU per-region write-through cache with backing persistent store (Postgres or RocksDB) for long TTLs
Dedup semantics: exact-match on canonical key OR explicit server-side body-hash match; return HTTP 409/202 semantics (202 Accepted + dedup-info) when duplicate detected

Timeout interaction: SDKs must expose 'cumulativeTimeout' config which represents the total wall-clock window for retries (includes hedged fanout), runtime enforces that cumulativeTimeout <= request-level SLO budget

qa_plan: Unit tests for canonicalization and header parsing
Integration: synthetic client that issues hedged requests with controlled region delays and asserts single side-effect
Chaos: region partitioning test during canary rollout (Dedicated staging) to validate duplicate rate below 0.1%
Regression: ensure existing non-idempotent endpoints remain unchanged unless opt-in
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Beta SDK release + runtime opt-in flag (2 weeks) - small set of internal customers
Phase 2: Gradual enablement for free-tier customers behind feature flag (4 weeks) - monitor dedup metrics
Phase 3: Default-on for all hosted customers with 30-day grace period and opt-out for enterprise (6 weeks)
Emergency rollback: runtime flag to disable hedged fanout and dedup enforcement immediately
communication: Announcement draft for Developers: includes migration guide and example canonicalization code
Support playbook: how to diagnose duplicates and key collision cases
Internal runbook: steps to toggle runtime flags and assess metrics during incidents
